name: The Barrens
summary: Across The Barrens, Horde outposts guard the roads as rival forces press in from every side. Once forest before the Great Sundering, this central Kalimdor plain is now dry country of red dust, scrub, and wandering wildlife. The Crossroads anchors Horde traffic, but quilboar, centaur, and creeping corruption threaten its hold.

sections.title: Heart of the New Horde
sections.body:
For generations, tauren nomads hunted kodo and zhevra across these plains. They also fought a recurring defensive war against the Kolkar centaur. During the Third War, Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor. He helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive back the centaur, then crossed the savanna into Mulgore with him. The Barrens now links Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.

The Crossroads and Camp Taurajo guard trade along the Gold Road. Orcish homesteads endure the harsh climate as the Horde builds a lasting home.

sections.title: A Land Under Siege
sections.body: Horde control of the savanna remains contested. Razormane quilboar raid farms and supply lines from thorn-choked strongholds, their bristles like porcupine quills. To the south, the dens of Razorfen Kraul loom over the land. On the eastern coast, Theramore forces hold Northwatch Hold, while dwarven prospectors dig into the titan complex of Bael Modan. Ratchet's goblins keep uneasy neutrality in trade and welcome travelers who bring coin.

sections.title: The Emerald Corruption
sections.body: Oases break up the northern plains, their waters surging with unnatural vigor. Their source lies in the Wailing Caverns, where the night elf druid Naralex sought the Emerald Dream and hoped to restore the Barrens to its ancient forested state. A nightmare twisted his vision. Now corrupted water flows through the Forgotten Pools and Stagnant Oasis, giving rise to strange deviate plants, unnatural beasts, and the rogue Druids of the Fang.

faq.q: Why are there lush oases in the middle of a desert?
aliases: why is there water in barrens
faq.answer: The Forgotten Pools and Lushwater Oasis draw water from underground springs flowing out of the Wailing Caverns. Night elf druid Naralex tried to channel those springs through the Emerald Dream and green the dry land. His effort went awry, filling the northern Barrens with potent, volatile natural magic.

The Horde garrisons the Crossroads, chiefly with orc and tauren warriors who serve Warchief Thrall. The main trade routes meet there, making it the Horde's chief military and transit hub in central Kalimdor. From the Crossroads, those routes link Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.

faq.q: Why are the quilboar attacking everyone?
faq.answer: The quilboar claim the Barrens as their ancestral birthright. They believe its great brambles grew from the blood of their demigod, Agamaggan, during the War of the Ancients. To them, the arriving Horde and native tauren are trespassers taking sacred foraging grounds and hunting territory.

faq.q: Why are Alliance soldiers in the Barrens?
faq.answer: The Alliance holds to the savanna's edges. Human troops from Theramore garrison Northwatch Hold to watch Horde movements. In the southern hills, dwarves at Bael Modan and Bael'dun Keep dig for ancient titan artifacts.

faq.q: Is Ratchet part of the Horde?
faq.answer: No. Ratchet is an independent goblin port run by Gazlowe. It welcomes Horde and Alliance travelers, smugglers, and adventurers for maritime trade, so long as they respect goblin commerce and keep weapons sheathed in town.

faq.q: What is going on with the silithid in the south?
faq.answer: Silithid have emerged from earthen hives in the southern Barrens, especially around the Field of Giants. These insect-like creatures have arrived suddenly, and their colonies are growing fast. They threaten travelers and nearby outposts, while the Horde investigates their origins.

angles.text: The Barrens is your realm's supply road. Hold the Crossroads and guard convoys along the Gold Road to help Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff endure.
Your nomadic ancestors roamed these savannas for generations before the orcs reached Kalimdor. They hunted sacred game and struggled to survive against the ruthless Kolkar centaur.
The altered waters of the Wailing Caverns mark a tragedy. Naralex's attempt to restore the Barrens fell to a nightmare.
These dry plains test your bond with the elements, from the spirits of parched earth to enchanted waters bubbling up in isolated oases.
